# [STORY] As a user, I want voice control to reliably understand English and German, including regional accents and dialects, so that I can use voice commands with my own accent

## User Story
**As a** user
**I want** voice control to reliably understand English and German, including regional accents and dialects
**So that** I can use voice commands even though my English/German isn't standard American, British, or literary-German pronunciation

## Acceptance Criteria (Given/When/Then)
- [ ] Given a user selects English or German from a language switch, when they dictate a command, then transcription runs against that language's speech model
- [ ] Given a user with a non-native or regional accent dictates a supported command in their selected language, when transcribed, then the correct command is recognized, verified against a documented set of accented/dialectal test recordings, not just standard-pronunciation samples
- [ ] Given transcript phrasing varies from the exact command phrases ("switch to light mode" vs. "light mode please"), when parsed, then the command is still correctly recognized via LLM-based intent parsing, not brittle regex
- [ ] Given a command genuinely can't be recognized after a good-faith attempt, when that happens, then the user sees the raw transcript and a clear "no matching command" message, same as today — must not regress
- [ ] Given the language switch changes, when the next voice command is dictated, then it uses the newly selected language end-to-end; mic capture is unaffected, only the STT locale changes

## Notes
Root cause: `SpeechToTextService` loaded a single small English Vosk model, and `voiceCommands.js` matched transcripts with English-only regex. Model coverage and phrasing tolerance are separate failure modes, so they are separate Tasks. Must stay inside ADR-004's $0/offline constraint — no cloud STT.

#212 closed: English (`vosk-model-en-us-0.22-lgraph`) and German (`vosk-model-small-de-0.15`) load independently, keyed by a `language` param defaulting to English. Model choice per ADR-021.

#216 closed: full-pipeline tests plus README/ARCHITECTURE.md updates.

Still blocking this Story: #215 (accented/dialectal test fixture, needs real audio) and #229 (real Vosk SHA256 checksums, needs a network-enabled machine).
